text:
marco: FYI CI linkcheck just flagged several links after running the mkdocs->docusaurus migration. Most are intra-site anchors that used to work.

build-bot: docs/linkcheck job #224 failed — 7 broken anchors. Artifacts: https://ci.redwood.ai/artifacts/docs/linkcheck/224

tara: quick repro: mkdocs slug for a heading 'Quickstart — embed() example' was `quickstart-embed-example` but docusaurus/mdx produced `quickstart---embed()` (keeps parens and em-dash). Our existing links point to the mkdocs form.

eli: I also found a weird one with non-latin headings: '国际指南' got slugified differently by the two toolchains. MkDocs used a transliteration, docusaurus kept unicode. So links like `#guoji-zhinan` vs `#国际指南`.

marco: options: 1) add redirects for old anchors (ugly but fast), 2) normalize slugs in the build (preferred), 3) update every link target (tedious).

tara: for speed I added a small redirect mapping in the docusaurus config and patched the most trafficked pages: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4420 (hotfix). Preview created.

build-bot: deploy preview for PR 4420: https://deploy-preview-4420--docs.redwood.ai. Running linkcheck on preview.

eli: for a durable solution I'm prototyping a small script that parses all headings across the repo and emits a mapping from mkdocs-slug -> current-slug so we can auto-generate redirects or update links in bulk. Will push as a tool in scripts/.

marco: can we add a lint that warns when authors put inline code or punctuation-heavy headings? That reduces future drift.

tara: yes, adding a docs-lint rule now. Also adding guidance in docs/authoring.md: prefer plain text headings or add an explicit id with HTML if you need special characters.

eli: note on i18n: any normalization must be careful with translated headings. Suggest we favor preserving unicode for translated pages but provide transliterated redirects for old mkdocs links.

i18n-bot: Added a task to the i18n backlog: check anchor stability across locales.

marco: plan: merge the hotfix redirects first (4420), then land the slug-normalizer tool + lint (PR forthcoming). After that run a full site linkcheck and run the scripts to emit redirects for any remaining mismatches.

tara: thanks — I'll monitor the preview and follow up if new failures pop up.
